title.narrative: Provision of an integrated nutrition lifesaving services to drought affected communities and IDPs in Jowhar district middle shabelle region.

description.narrative:
ltp class="" style=""gtltspan style="font-size: 10pt"gt To avert worsening nutrition situation in Jowhar, PDA will implement life-saving malnutrition prevention and treatment interventions including mass screening of children 6-59 months and PLWs and appropriate referral for care and treatment, Integrated care and treatment of severe acute malnutrition through both static and outreach clinics in IDP camps and in underserved and hard to reach areas in communities with Fixed health centres in lt/spangtltspan style="font-size: 14px"gtRAQAYLE, MOHAMED FARAH, PRIMO ZENDO, LIBEGA, HANSHOLEY mobile teams and GEDO BARKAN, BAYHAWO static OTP sites lt/spangtltspan style="font-size: 14px"gtlocations Jowhar district,. The project will contribute to scale up nutrition services for early malnutrition cases detection and timely treatment and referrals where necessary to avoid morbidities and mortalities related to malnutrition. The project targets the most affected people who are pregnant and lactating women and under 5 children who bear the brunt of the protracted emergency in Somalia. The project will screen, treat and refer 7,000 under 5 children and 6800 PLWs in Jowhar district from both IDP camps and surrounding host community for acute malnutrition and offer treatment and care to 2450 and 3368 under 5 children for moderate and severe acute malnutrition respectively. PDAlt/spangtltspan style="font-size: 14px"gt lt/spangtltspan style="font-size: 14px"gt lt/spangtltspan style="font-size: 14px"gtwill work closely with UNICEF and WFP to ensure 4420lt/spangtltspan style="font-size: 14px color: red"gt lt/spangtltspan style="font-size: 14px"gtpregnant and lactating women are connected to the MCHN programmes and receive multiple micronutrients. The project will also look into the bottle necks by addressing socio-cultural barriers which hinder utilization of available health and nutrition services such as health seeking behavior of the local communities. The project will also work towards strengthening human resources for health and nutrition by engaging in capacity building initiatives. The health facility staff engaged in service provision will be trained on various thematic areas (e.g. IMAM and IYCF). The project will also ensure the benefits of working with community structures such as the Community nutrition workers (CNWs) and Community nutrition champions to be able to address the nutrition needs of vulnerable groups, PDA will also ensure integrationlt/spangtltspan style="font-size: 14px"gt lt/spangtltspan style="font-size: 14px"gtof gender base violence, child protection and PSEA mainstreaming within the nutrition project intervention service to enable prevention, referral and case managementlt/spangtltspan style="font-size: 14px"gt lt/spangtltspan style="font-size: 14px"gtof GBV/Child protection and PSEA among the nutrition staff and community nutrition volunteerslt/spangtlt/pgtltp class="" style=""gt
